title: StepManifest
description: The DATA face of one step in the orchestrator's standard (Template Method) execution: its logical inputs, its outputs (with validator NAMES resolved from the code registry), its routing map, its agent levers, and any post-turn CLIs. The StepExecutor reads this to drive the fixed phases; only validator fn bodies and the agent spawn stay code.

match.description: How an action maps to this manifest: a STRICT SUBSET of a WorkflowAction. Every field present here must equal the action's field for a match. The loader rejects an ambiguous overlap (two manifests matching one action).

inputs.description: The logical inputs the orchestrator resolves from .consort and PROVIDES to the step (contents, keyed by id).

id.description: Logical input id the contents are handed back under.

preconditions.description: The pre-conditions the orchestrator PREPARES (via the preparer registry) and appends to the step's prompt before dispatch: the pre-extracted context-pack (rubric + module layout) and, for assess, the green-failure advisory. LOGICAL (by kind), never authored, projected deterministically from on-disk .consort. Absent = an affirmative 'nothing'; a declared preparer that yields empty is logged as an anomaly.

id.description: Key the prepared block is handed back under.

kind.description: Preparer kind resolved from the preparer registry (context-pack | green-failure-advisory).

options.description: Preparer-specific knobs, e.g. { "skipTestLoop": true } for context-pack.

outputs.description: The logical outputs the step produces into its workspace. Each declares an in-code conformance validator BY NAME (resolved from validator-registry.ts). May be empty for a turn verified by cycle records rather than a static artifact.

filename.description: Artifact filename within the provided workspace.

validator.description: Registered OutputValidator name (validator-registry.ts). resolveValidator throws loud on an unknown name.

channel.description: WHICH channel this output lands in (absent = the primary workspace root, byte-identical to a single-root turn). product = the application deliverable that accumulates across build turns + gets committed/migrated/deployed (app/, tests/, migrations); MUST be uncontained (the real code tree; a per-experiment worktree when experiments run in parallel), since each build turn reads prior turns' code. artifact = the .consort design documents (feature-spec/architecture/test-list/design-guide) the design roles author; small + per-feature, so it MAY be contained (resolved under artifactDir when the orchestrator provisions one, else the workspace). meta = the orchestrator's bookkeeping about the turn (raw agent report, reflect verdict, assess marker), whose CONFORMANCE the orchestrator owns; contained (resolved under metaDir when provisioned, else the workspace). Each root defaults to workspaceDir, so an untagged / un-provisioned turn is byte-identical.

routing.description: The routing proposal map keyed by StepOutcome. Each outcome maps to a next-move descriptor the contract's route() emits; the orchestrator's validateAndBound reconciles it with the pure allowed transition. A produced route of "state-derived" defers entirely to the pure transition.

agentOptions.description: The agent levers the StepExecutor builds AgentLevers from for the dispatch-agent phase.

postTurn.description: Role-specific deterministic CLIs run in the record/log phase (reset/sync-breakdown, test-list, cycle stamps).

agent.description: WHICH concrete StepAgent this step uses + that agent's config, resolved via the agent catalogue. `kind` names a catalogue entry (claude | replay | mock); `config` is that kind's knobs. The ENV a kind needs (corpus root, kit dir) is supplied by the runner, NOT here.

kind.description: Catalogue kind: claude (real spawn) | replay (recorded artifacts) | mock (fixtures).

config.description: The kind's own config (claude levers / replay seeds / mock outputs).

routeTarget.description: Where an outcome proposes to go. Either a concrete WorkflowAction under `next`, the sentinel string "state-derived" (defer to the pure transition), or a bare flag object (retry/gate) the contract interprets.
